_what: Roles that are supposed to have a live node behind them, and why. A role that quietly empties looks exactly like a role that is working: the policy still names it, the tests still pass, and a drill against it returns a reassuring zero. This file is what roles_check.py compares the live network against (D-076).

expected_live.tag:gateway-home: The only way into the house. If this is empty nothing in the home network is reachable at all.
expected_live.tag:prod: The production stand-in, and the host two projects run on.
expected_live.tag:collector: The telemetry sink. An empty collector loses readings silently -- the hub keeps pushing into nothing.
expected_live.tag:appliance: The test user's only destination, and the intended standby route into the house. It went offline for six days after a system update and nobody noticed (D-076).

expected_empty.tag:sensor: Declared, not built -- simulated sensors are deferred.
expected_empty.tag:drone: Declared and deliberately never filled: nothing outside the house may move the robot.
expected_empty.tag:gateway-standby: Waiting on the appliance's routes being narrowed and approved (D-069).
expected_empty.tag:workstation: Filled 2026-09-22; kept here until it has been live for a week, since a work machine may legitimately be switched off.
